page: Google Cloud Platform g4-standard-48 is an x86_64 architecture server configured with 48 dedicated vCPUs and 180.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.75 GB of RAM per core. The instance features a single NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 GPU from the Ada Lovelace family, providing 96 GB of dedicated VRAM.

This server configuration does not include local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes. Additionally, the instance does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The hardware profile balances a high-capacity 96 GB GPU VRAM buffer with 48 dedicated vCPUs, offering a specialized resource density for graphics-intensive workloads, 3D rendering, and model inference. The lack of local storage and public IPv4 addresses represents a structural tradeoff that requires external provisioning, which influences the overall deployment architecture and resource-density cost considerations.
description: Google Cloud Platform g4-standard-48 is an x86_64 architecture server optimized for graphics-intensive workloads. The instance is configured with 48 dedicated vCPUs and 180.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 3.75 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 GPU from the Ada Lovelace architecture family, featuring 96 GB of dedicated VRAM. This server does not include local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be fulfilled through network-attached volumes. It also includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The high VRAM capacity relative to the system memory and CPU cores makes this server suitable for workloads such as 3D rendering, visualization, and machine learning inference where large model weights or textures must reside directly in the GPU frame buffer.
